sources.attribution: Nippon Paper Industries Co., Ltd.; Getworks Co., Ltd.; Tokyo Gas Engineering Solutions Corporation
sources.summary: Joint release of Getworks, Tokyo Gas Engineering Solutions (TGES) and Nippon Paper, dated 5 November 2026 on Nippon Paper's newsroom. The three companies have signed contracts on land use and power supply to carry out a container data-centre business at Nippon Paper's Kushiro works (日本製紙釧路事業所). Getworks is the data-centre operator and plans, designs, builds and operates the container data centre; TGES coordinates the business and designs and builds the foundations, water supply and electrical works; Nippon Paper provides the land (釧路事業所用地) and supplies power from the existing receiving and generating plant at the works. It is the first project under the Getworks-TGES alliance of 14 September 2026. The companies plan 6 MW in operation within FY2026 and expansion to about 40 MW in September 2027, and regard the site as having potential for up to 150 MW, with gas-fired distributed generation under consideration. Nippon Paper notes that the Kushiro works ended paper production in 2021 and continues its power-generation business. The operating dates and capacities are plans, not observations.

sources.summary: Telehouse's release dated 29 October 2026 states that KDDI Corporation and Telehouse International Corporation of Europe Limited have completed the purchase of the Inventory Estate in East India Dock, London, from LaSalle Investment Management and Trilogy Real Estate for more than £220 million (US$294 million). The land will support a new high-density, AI-ready data centre as part of the expansion of Telehouse's existing London Docklands campus, whose connectivity ecosystem the release describes as operating at the campus; the planned development is to offer high-density colocation, low-latency connectivity and AI workloads, and 65 MVA of power has been secured for the site for phased, long-term expansion. The release says the new data centre will be one of the largest facilities in the Telehouse London Docklands campus, and separately describes Telehouse West Two as a nine-storey building currently in development at the campus, due for completion in 2028. Telehouse and KDDI executives and a LaSalle representative are quoted; their names are not reproduced here.
